_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. A mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so the oracle registration and the catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `en1996-1-any` is generated from each triad leaf's own `SemanticDescriptor.kind`, in `#[derive(dsl::Mutations)]`'s declaration order, and `kinds_match_the_enum_and_the_catalog` in `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs` fails the moment this list and the enum part company.

oracles.rationale:
🐍️ No third-party library in any ecosystem reads or writes `s.norm.en1996` — checked against PyPI, which serves no `en1996`, `eurocode`, `vdi3805` or `iso16757` distribution, and whose nearest real packages (`structuralcodes`, `concreteproperties`, `anastruct`) implement design-code formulae and speak no interchange format — so this subset's reference is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION rather than a third-party distribution. That is why `package` is empty: the entry links no external library and contributes nothing to the dependency ratchet. The implementation is `../🧪️tests/🪨️mutate-en1996-1/🐍️.py` (engine `✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️execution/🐍️.py`), all 58 kinds of `En1996Mutation` written in Python from `26/08/12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL`'s `📓️taxonomy.md` (verb table, the `new_<field>` naming mechanic, the addressing convention) and `📓️derivation-rules.md` (shape rules), plus this manifest's own catalog for the closed list of kinds. It imports nothing from the Rust it judges and transliterates none of it — the field a `new*` argument names is resolved by normalised spelling against the document's own keys, exactly as the naming mechanic states. Its reading is pinned by reaching every committed handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` vector and by re-emitting the committed `.dsl.semio` artifact byte for byte, neither of which a misreading could do.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `en1996-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 58-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

oracles.rationale: 🐍️ Independent-formulation compliance oracle of EN1996: the python compliance script reads its own independently keyed table file (`⚖️compliance/📚️tables.json`) and recomputes the wall utilisations by brute-force enumeration of the EN 1990 combinations. For the catalogue it uses third-party numerics: scipy bilinear interpolation for the EN 772-1 shape factor, shapely facet geometry with scipy minimisation for the Johansen yield-line load of laterally loaded panels (per-line orthotropic rule, not the projection formula of the Rust code), scipy root finding for the three-hinge arching statics and the reinforced-masonry equilibrium, and numpy fibre integration for the M-N diagram. Closed-form entries without a library (f_k, Phi, beta, fire rows) are labelled independent formulation. The oracle exchanges everything through stdin and stdout and writes no file. The shared harness (`✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️harness`) replays blessed oracle cases against the third-party references claimed in the norm root registry (`norm-eurocode-structuralcodes`, `-concreteproperties`, `-sectionproperties`, `-blue-prints`, `-sympy`, `-groundhog`, scipy numerics). Labelled honestly as independent formulation, not third-party validation, wherever no library covers the clause. Wave 2 doc oracles v2: the document-level oracle `🚦️check-outcome/🐍️.py` wraps the compression, mid-height, slenderness and simplified rows and adds the declared eccentricity 6.1.2.2, shear and sliding 6.2, lateral flexure 6.3 and the concentrated load with its area rule 6.1.3 per load case; `--self-check` validates the wall section modulus against sectionproperties, the wind moment against PyNite and the bearing factor cap against scipy.optimize.

Reference values of the EN1996 oracle case files (`🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🔮️oracle-cases/third-party*.json`) for the checks en1996.6.6.1.flexure-reinforced are computed by concreteproperties 0.8.0. The harness adapter `✏️s/🔌️plugins/📕️norm/🔮️oracles/🏃️harness/🔌️adapters/concreteproperties/🐍️.py` is the only importer; values are blessed from the library, never from the Rust. National Annex parameters are inputs of the cases.
